ASST: Strive, Inc. (Nasdaq: ASST) is a company that holds bitcoin on its balance sheet — a "bitcoin treasury" company — and also sells asset-management services. The ASST ticker belonged to Asset Entities Inc. before a merger in September 2025, so share prices from before that date are not comparable with today's. Accounting rules also require Strive to report bitcoin at its current market value, so reported earnings swing with the bitcoin price. On 2026-10-15 the shares rose 3.89%, and over three months they are up 107.7%. The screen tag "Up / cooling" means the earlier gain is slowing, not reversing. **The bullish mechanism.** Strive pays for bitcoin mostly with preferred stock — a class of share that pays a fixed dividend and ranks ahead of common stock for payouts — instead of issuing new common shares. That avoids diluting the common shares (spreading ownership thinner) and raises the amount of bitcoin behind each common share, as long as bitcoin's return beats the dividend cost. Two things support this. First, Strive bought 3,311 bitcoin for about $280 million at roughly $84,500 per coin between 5 and 9 October 2026, taking holdings to 32,773 bitcoin ([Strive Acquires 3,311 Bitcoins At Average Price Of $84,500 Per Bitcoin From Oct. 5 Through Oct. 9](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62320971/strive-acquires-3-311-bitcoins-average-price-84-500-bitcoin-oct-5-through-oct-9)). Second, it announced — but has not completed — an initial public offering of 5 million SATS preferred shares at $100 each, to raise $500 million, paying a 15% dividend and ranking behind the existing SATA preferred ([Strive Plans To Conduct Initial Public Offering Of 5M Shares Of Its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Shares](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62341031/strive-plans-conduct-initial-public-offering-5m-shares-its-15-series-perpetual-sats-preferred-shares); [Strive (ASST) aims to raise $500 million with SATS preferred offering](https://coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/13/strive-to-ipo-second-preferred-share-class-as-it-looks-to-further-build-bitcoin-treasury)). The stated uses of the money are more bitcoin, income-producing assets, or share buybacks. A brokerage research note from TD Cowen projects bitcoin at $132,750 by 2028 and says Strive could outperform (TD Cowen: Bitcoin to Hit $132,750 by 2028, Strategy, Strive Could Outperform). **The bearish mechanism.** The preferred shares sit ahead of the common stock. SATA pays about 13% (variable) and SATS would pay 15%, so together they would absorb roughly $75 million a year in fixed dividends before a common holder receives anything. If bitcoin is flat or falls, the leftover value tilts to the preferred holders. Three facts cut against the bull case. The weekly regulatory filings do not add up: the reported weeks sum to about 6,242 bitcoin, short of the 7,773-coin increase in holdings, so one report is missing, and the source of the money used to buy the bitcoin is not disclosed. In one August 2026 window, holdings grew 5.5% while bitcoin per diluted share grew only 1.3% — growth that did not reach common holders one-for-one. Momentum is also cooling. A 2x ASST fund (a fund that aims to double the daily ASST move) adds flow-driven price swings, but it magnifies only its own returns, not the company's ([Wall Street ETF Factory Goes Wild: 3X Bets, AI Fever and 1,100 New Funds](https://benzinga.com/etfs/broad-u-s-equity-etfs/26/10/62339186/wall-streets-etf-factory-is-going-wild-3x-bets-ai-fever-and-1100-new-funds)). **Which thesis the facts favor.** The bull mechanism, mildly, but not decisively. The purchases are verified, the funding plan is sized, and an outside analyst case supports it. The number that settles the question is bitcoin per ASST share after the purchases and the raise, compared with the share price. If the shares cost less than the bitcoin behind them, that is a discount; if they cost more, that is a premium. The bull thesis fails if bitcoin per share stops rising, if the SATS offering is cut, or if the common stock trades below the value of its bitcoin. The bear thesis fails if bitcoin rallies well past recent purchase prices, or if the proceeds are held or used for buybacks rather than spent. Facts to obtain next: the missing weekly purchase report, the source of the funding already used, and the current count of common shares outstanding.

CORZ: **Answer: For one week and one month, neither the bull nor the bear case has a clean edge. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, but the bull case is not disproved. The decisive year-ahead question is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases.** **Company identity.** Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) is a bitcoin miner that now sells high-density data-center space. That business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI and high-performance computing customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024. CoreWeave agreed to acquire Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (CoreWeave to acquire Core Scientific, company press release). That deal did not complete. A retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination timing as unverified. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ. **Price move.** On 15 October 2026, CORZ rose 7.1% on the day. But it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months, and -27.5% over one year. The day's gain came against a falling semiconductor and AI-hardware tape driven by rate-hike fears (Rate Pressure vs. AI Demand: Rising Treasury Yields Trigger Nvidia, AMD Slump). Similar single-day gains in Cipher and TeraWulf look like a catalyst-free oversold bounce. Treat 15 October as group mean-reversion in beaten-down miner and data-center names until a company-specific driver appears. Do not use the 7-8 October price points in the retained snippets: one says CORZ fell 4.4% to $15.94 on 2026-10-07, another says it closed down 3.67% at $18.10 on 2026-10-08. These cannot both be right, so no price level should be taken from them. **Shared driver, not company failure.** The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders. On 7-8 October, Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose ([IREN Falls 7% as Financing-Heavy Data Center Names Sell Off Apart From Their Sector Fund; TeraWulf and Core Scientific Drop 5%](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/07/iren-falls-7-as-financing-heavy-data-center-names-sell-off-apart-from-their-sector-fund-terawulf-and-core-scientific-drop-5)). Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate ([CoreWeave Stock Keeps Sinking As Wall Street Questions Its Debt-Fueled AI Empire](https://benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62378700/coreweave-stock-keeps-sinking-as-wall-street-questions-its-debt-fueled-ai-empire)) and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. This matters because Core Scientific must borrow to build. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion ([Capital Over Chips: Broadcom CEO Warns Financing Costs Could Slow AI Expansion](https://benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62379402/capital-over-chips-broadcom-ceo-warns-financing-costs-could-slow-ai-expansion)). **Reported results for the quarter ended 2026-06-30.** Revenue was $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M a year earlier. Operating income was +$20.7M. Gross profit was $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was $41.1M. Liquidity was $1.82B ([Core Scientific Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/139/core-scientific-announces-second-quarter-2026-results)). The build-out is the dominant financial fact: total assets rose to $5.26B from $3.07B at 31 March 2026, and total liabilities rose to $7.68B from $4.38B. **Read the cash flow correctly.** Free cash flow was -$1.02B in Q2 2026. This is a quarterly figure. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Most of the -$1.02B is capital spending, because operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive. The funding need is growth investment, not operating losses. That single quarter's outflow is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025. The money comes from outside the business: a $3.3B 7.75% senior secured notes offering described in the Q1 2026 release ([Core Scientific Announces First Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/136/core-scientific-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-results)); $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities reported 14 September 2026 ([Core Scientific (CORZ) lines up fresh credit to free cash for AI infrastructure](https://stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CORZ/8-k-core-scientific-inc-tx-reports-material-event-a86a4bdfb955.html)); and conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas sites on 14 September 2026 ([Core Scientific wins conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data centers](https://tradingview.com/news/tradingview:b55357bd92728:0-core-scientific-wins-conditional-ercot-power-approvals-for-texas-data-centers)). ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions. **Negative equity.** Stockholders' equity was -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are greater than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event. Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026. That swing points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss. The binding constraints are liquidity and continued access to debt and equity on acceptable terms. **Bull case, mechanism and support.** Core Scientific owns low-cost power and land. Converting it to high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt and per dollar invested once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin. On 28 July 2026, the company announced an AMD partnership covering 500+ MW of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW. MW means megawatt, a unit of power. GW means gigawatt, 1,000 megawatts. ERCOT conditional approvals support the Texas pipeline. Assumption: the pipeline becomes signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt. Invalidation: announcements do not turn into contracts with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates; or leasing rents and utilization fall short of the cost of capital. **Bear case, mechanism and support.** A capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads, or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow, $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets, negative equity, and demonstrated sensitivity to financing news. Counterevidence that weakens it: the recent fall is sector- and rate-driven rather than a CORZ-specific operating failure. The only company-specific October item in the evidence is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05: Investing.com India: Core Scientific Officer Todd Duchene Sells $163,055 in Stock). That sale is too small to explain the decline. **Verdict by horizon.** For one week and one month, neither side has a clean edge. The direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates, which the company does not control. Note that Q2 2026 results were reported on 28 July 2026, so a Q3 2026 report is likely within the one-month window, even though the confirmed date is not in the evidence. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The decisive variable over a year is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases. **What to obtain next.** The CoreWeave deal termination date. Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates. The Q3 2026 report date and results. The leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.

MRNA: # Moderna (MRNA) research brief **Answer first.** Moderna is a commercial-stage maker of mRNA vaccines. Over the next year, the established business facts favor the bullish case. Over the next three months, neither side has a reliable edge, because the recent price gain came mainly from index buying and from a government programme that starts in December. Over five years, neither case has an edge yet. **What the company sells.** Approved products are Spikevax for COVID-19, mRESVIA for RSV, and mFLUSIVA for seasonal influenza. The flu vaccine won FDA approval on 5 August 2026 after a unanimous advisory-committee vote in June 2026 ([Moderna Announces FDA Advisory Committee Votes Unanimously in Favor of the Benefit-Risk Profile of mRNA-1010, an Investigational Seasonal Influenza Vaccine](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/moderna-announces-fda-advisory-committee-200000554.html)). Its most valuable pipeline asset is intismeran autogene, also called mRNA-4157 or V940. It is a personalised cancer vaccine partnered with Merck. Sales are seasonal. COVID and RSV vaccine sales rise in fall and winter, so Q3 and Q4 carry the year. **Latest quarter and cash.** The quarter ended 30 June 2026 was reported on 31 July 2026. Revenue was $145M, up 2.1% from a year earlier. Net loss was $782M. Operating cash flow was -$526M. Free cash flow was -$563M. Stockholders equity was $6.76B against $4.20B of liabilities ([Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA) Q2 2026 loss, trims 2026 spending](https://stocktitan.net/sec-filings/MRNA/8-k-moderna-inc-reports-material-event-e26a8178aec3.html), [Moderna Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Updates](https://accessnewswire.com/newsroom/en/healthcare-and-pharmaceutical/moderna-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-bu-1199078)). The company cut its 2026 cost and research outlook, repeated a plan for up to 10% revenue growth, and guided to $4.7-5.2B of year-end cash. Seasonality is the key to reading these numbers. Q2 revenue of $145M and first-half revenue of $534M say little about the full year, because Q3 2025 revenue was $1,016M. The next real test is the Q3 2026 report, expected 6 November 2026. **The price move.** MRNA closed at $221.16 on 9 October 2026. It was roughly 14% higher that day, +61.9% over 21 days, and +230.1% over 63 days, with a 14-day RSI of 71.2 and 20% annualised volatility of 80.5%. It remained 54.4% below its $484.65 all-time high ([Moderna, Inc. (MRNA) Stock Price, News, Quote & History](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRNA)). The supplied observations for 15 October 2026 show +4.82% on the day, +297.4% over three months, +753.3% over one year, and -22.5% over five years. A separate 15 October record puts the day at +5.52%. Treat the day figure as approximately +5% and note the two readings. **What drove the multi-month move, as reported.** At least three reported drivers ran in sequence. First, on 19 August 2026 Merck and Moderna announced positive topline Phase 3 results for intismeran autogene plus KEYTRUDA in completely resected Stage IIB-IV melanoma. The trial met recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival endpoints. Press coverage credits that result with nearly doubling the stock ([Merck and Moderna Announce Phase 3 INTerpath-001 Trial of Intismeran Autogene Plus KEYTRUDA Met Endpoints of Recurrence-Free Survival and Distant Metastasis-Free Survival in Patients With Completely Resected Stage IIB-IV Melanoma](https://businesswire.com/news/home/20260819675697/en/Merck-and-Moderna-Announce-Phase-3-INTerpath-001-Trial-of-Intismeran-Autogene-Plus-KEYTRUDA-Met-Endpoints-of-Recurrence-Free-Survival-RFS-and-Distant-Metastasis-Free-Survival-DMFS-in-Patients-With-Completely-Resected-Stage-IIB-IV-Melanoma), [INTerpath-001 Trial of mRNA-Based Individualized Neoantigen Therapy Meets Primary and Key Secondary Endpoints in Patients With High-Risk Resected Melanoma](https://ascopost.com/news/august-2026/interpath-001-trial-of-mrna-based-individualized-neoantigen-therapy-meets-primary-and-key-secondary-endpoints-in-patients-with-high-risk-resected-melanoma)). Second, Nasdaq said on 1 October that MRNA would rejoin the Nasdaq-100 before the open on 9 October, replacing Warner Bros. Discovery. That is real but one-time index-fund buying ([Moderna (NASDAQ:MRNA) Stock Surges 14% as Nasdaq-100 Return and Cancer Vaccine Hopes Fuel Rally](https://stocksdownunder.com/moderna-stock-surges-nasdaq-100-cancer-vaccine)). Third, on 9 October a National Institutes of Health-backed public-private cancer-vaccine programme lifted MRNA, BioNTech, and Novavax. It targets pancreatic, liver, and colorectal cancers first and is expected to start in December 2026. The first driver is an operating fact. The second is mechanical fund flow. The third is sentiment with no revenue attached (MRNA October 9, 2026 surge: Nasdaq-100 reentry and NIH cancer-vaccine report; MRNA: October 2026 cancer-vaccine and Nasdaq-100 news rally). **Three-month hypothesis, to mid-January 2027.** The bull mechanism: the 6 November Q3 report should show the seasonal step-up toward the roughly $1B Q3 2025 level, and mFLUSIVA adds a third approved product into the same fall window. The bear mechanism: the October gain came from index buying and a programme that starts in December, momentum is stretched above RSI 70, and the company still consumes cash. The year-end cash guide of $4.7-5.2B implies further consumption in the second half relative to the $6.9B of cash and investments at 30 June 2026, although those two figures may not be defined identically. The $950M litigation payment also falls in that window. Counterevidence for the bear case: the company funded itself in August 2026 with an upsized convertible offering, so it faces no near-term funding stress. Reported terms: proposed 27 August 2026 at $2.0B, priced 28 August 2026 at $2.6B, with net proceeds of about $2.957B after full exercise of the purchasers option and $328.8M spent on capped calls. One secondary report describes $3.0B of zero-coupon notes due 2032, which is consistent with a fully exercised option, but the retained filing record did not contain coupon, maturity, or conversion terms (Moderna $2.6B convertible senior notes offering (2026)). Verdict: the operating facts have not yet changed and the tape has, so neither side has a reliable edge on price alone over this window. Invalidation tests: Q3 2026 revenue materially below $1B or a guidance cut on 6 November for the bear case; a Q3 beat with a raised outlook or a regulatory filing acceptance for intismeran autogene for the bull case. **One-year hypothesis, to October 2027.** The bull mechanism: a positive Phase 3 with two endpoints in high-risk resected melanoma supports a regulatory submission in 2027. That would create a high-price oncology line and shift the revenue mix away from seasonal vaccines. The partner, Merck, has an existing checkpoint-inhibitor franchise and commercial reach. The bear mechanism: even an approval would be a small, slow revenue line against a shrinking COVID franchise. The pipeline also carries failures. The norovirus candidate mRNA-1403 missed statistical criteria at a Phase 3 interim analysis. An officer filed in September 2026 to sell about $5.88M of shares ([Another multimillion stock sale lined up for 2026 at Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA)](https://stocktitan.net/sec-filings/MRNA/144-moderna-inc-sec-filing-d0826d66ef29.html)). Verdict: the business facts favor the bull case. A Phase 3 that hit two endpoints, an approved flu vaccine, and a funded balance sheet are established facts, not forecasts. The bear case at this horizon rests mainly on valuation and on how quickly oncology revenue arrives, which is unknown. Observable invalidation: a regulatory delay or negative review, or no filing for intismeran autogene by mid-2027. **Five-year hypothesis, to 2031.** The bull mechanism: if mRNA works in oncology, the platform addresses many tumour types, and the NIH programme plus Mercks pipeline widen the market. The bear mechanism: equity has fallen from $11.9B in 2024Q3 to $6.76B in 2026Q2, the company has raised capital repeatedly, and reimbursement and manufacturing economics for personalised neoantigen therapy at scale are unproven. Verdict: neither thesis has an edge yet. **Two smaller corrections.** Flu is a third approved product after COVID and RSV, not a second. And distinguish reported facts from interpretation. The mapped drivers of the rally come from press reports and index notices, not from a single filing. The statement that the three-month move has priced in unearned revenue is interpretation, not an established fact. **Facts to obtain next.** What the late-October 2026 late-stage melanoma presentation contains and whether it is the INTerpath-001 dataset or a new one. The coupon, maturity, and conversion terms of the August 2026 converts, and the dilution they imply. The status and cash effect of the $950M litigation matter, since the $6.9B cash figure at 30 June 2026 predates it. Whether Merck has filed for approval of intismeran autogene. Whether the NIH cancer-vaccine programme creates procurement that reaches Moderna specifically. **Units and identity.** All figures are US dollars. Quarterly figures are calendar quarters from the supplied fundamentals. The rally percentages are price returns over the stated windows and are not comparable across sources when the end-date snapshot differs.

JBLU: # JetBlue Airways (JBLU) — grounded research brief, 16 October 2026 **Bottom line:** The facts available favour the bearish case for the near horizons (one week to three months), because the last reported quarter shows the loss widening while cash goes out and shareholders' equity shrinks, and because credit raters and analysts have moved the same way. The bullish case depends on a turnaround that has not yet shown up in reported numbers. The next hard fact arrives on 27 October 2026. ## What the company is and what happened to the price JetBlue is a United States passenger airline. It sells seats on domestic routes, to the Caribbean and Latin America, and across the Atlantic. Its profit depends on the money it collects per seat flown one mile against fuel, labour and airport costs. As of 15 October 2026 the shares had risen 4.66% in one day, but they were down 20.8% over one week, 29.2% over one month, 42.3% over three months, 36.5% over one year and 79.8% over five years. Every horizon is marked "Down / worsening". One strong day inside a falling month is not a turn. Two reports describe the slump. On 13 October 2026 the shares fell 4.78% to $3.19, and a Kalkine report linked the fall to a run of negative analyst revisions ([Why did JetBlue sink 4.78% to USD 3.19](https://kalkine.ca/news/travel/why-did-jetblue-airways-nasdaqjblu-sink-478-to-usd-319)). A 14 October 2026 report said the shares fell 7.31% on concern about rising operating costs and weakening demand as banks cut price targets ([JetBlue Airways news, 14 October 2026](https://stockstotrade.com/news/jetblue-airways-corporation-jblu-news-2026_10_14/)). The two reports do not agree on the size of the 14 October move, and neither states the period for its figure. Analyst actions in that window were all negative on price: Susquehanna cut its target to $4 from $6 and kept a Neutral rating, naming unit revenue trends into the fourth quarter as the critical watch point; Goldman Sachs cut to $3.50 from $4 with a Sell rating; TD Cowen stayed at Hold; BMO was named among banks cutting targets. These are analyst target changes, not company forecasts. ## Established business facts Reported quarterly figures to 2026Q2 (period ending 30 June 2026): - Revenue was $2.697bn, up about 14.5% from $2.356bn in 2025Q2. - Net loss was $247m, about three times wider than the $74m loss a year earlier. - Operating loss was $141m. - Free cash flow was negative $318m, and has been negative in every quarter shown from 2024Q4 onward. - Shareholders' equity fell from $2.641bn at 2024Q4 to $1.587bn at 2026Q2, while total liabilities rose to $14.784bn. A 13 October 2026 commentary noted the tension directly: the shares hit fresh 52-week lows even though second-quarter 2026 revenue and unit revenue grew, because losses widened as costs rose. Revenue growing while the loss widens means cost growth is running ahead of pricing. On credit, S&P Global Ratings lowered JetBlue to CCC+ from B- on 8 June 2026 with a stable outlook, citing elevated fuel costs and sustained high leverage ([JetBlue Financials: Losses, Debt & JetForward Turnaround](https://dwuconsulting.com/dwu-ai/jetblue-airways-financial-profile)). CCC+ is a rating grade that signals substantial credit risk. A separate CreditSights note frames cash burn and Middle East tensions as the drivers of liquidity concern, with financing options drawing focus ([JetBlue cash burn, Middle East tensions fuel liquidity concerns](https://know.creditsights.com/insights/us-special-situations-jetblue-cash-burn-middle-east-tensions-fuel-liquidity-concerns-as-financing-options-draw-focus/)). ## Bearish hypothesis **Mechanism:** Fuel, labour and airport costs rise faster than the money collected per seat mile. Revenue per seat grows, but the loss widens anyway, so the company keeps spending more cash than it earns. Falling equity and high leverage then make borrowing more expensive or force a share sale, which spreads the same profit over more shares. **Supporting facts:** Q2 2026 revenue up 14.5% but the loss about three times wider; negative free cash flow in every quarter shown; equity down about 40% from 2024Q4; the S&P downgrade to CCC+; negative analyst target revisions into 14 October 2026. **Assumption:** The cost trend of the last reported quarter continues into the third quarter. **Counterevidence:** Susquehanna kept a Neutral rating rather than Sell, and the 13 October commentary described the situation as a contrarian setup. Revenue and unit revenue did grow. **Observable invalidation:** The Q3 2026 report shows a narrower loss and unit revenue growth above unit cost growth; or no new financing is needed on expensive terms; or a credit rater lifts the outlook. ## Bullish hypothesis **Mechanism:** The JetForward turnaround pushes revenue up faster than costs. Higher revenue per seat then converts into a smaller loss rather than a wider one, and a stock near its 52-week low with a Sell rating already priced in re-rates when the loss narrows. **Supporting facts:** Revenue rose 14.5% year on year in 2026Q2 and unit revenue grew; the shares bounced 4.66% on 15 October 2026. **Assumption:** Fuel prices fall or capacity is cut enough that cost growth slows below revenue growth. **Counterevidence:** The loss widened in the same quarter that revenue grew, which is the opposite of the mechanism. Goldman Sachs carries a Sell rating, and S&P rates the debt CCC+. One up day inside a 42% three-month fall does not show a change in the business. **Observable invalidation:** The Q3 2026 report shows a further widening loss, or a new share issue or expensive borrowing, or another credit downgrade. ## Which thesis the facts favour The bearish thesis has the better support on the facts in hand, because the only reported quarter shows costs outrunning pricing while cash leaves the business, and because the credit and analyst moves point the same way. That is an edge on the reported trajectory, not a forecast. The bullish case rests on a turnaround that has not yet appeared in any reported number, so it is a claim about the future rather than a reading of the evidence. The edge is strongest over one week to three months and weakest over one year to five years, where the outcome depends on whether the turnaround ever produces positive free cash flow. That question is unresolved. ## Facts to obtain next - The third-quarter 2026 results, due on the call at 10:00 a.m. ET on 27 October 2026 (JetBlue Announces Webcast of Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call, 13 October 2026). Unit revenue against unit cost is the decisive comparison. - The company's stated full-year 2026 guidance and any capacity or route changes. - Total liquidity and the maturity schedule for the next twelve months, to test how far cash burn can continue without new funding. - The fuel hedge position and the current share count. - Whether the 13 and 14 October 2026 price falls had a company-specific trigger beyond the analyst revisions. This is research, not a recommendation to buy or sell.

CRGY: **Bottom line: the facts identify the catalyst and the mechanics clearly, but they do not yet support a directional edge for either side over the next week, month or quarter. The decisive numbers — what Crescent paid per unit of production, how the purchase was funded, and what the combined company earns per share — are not in the evidence.** **What the company is, and what just happened** Crescent Energy Company Class A common stock (ticker CRGY, SEC filer number CIK 1866175) is an independent oil and gas producer with assets in the Permian and Eagle Ford areas. It grows mainly by buying other producers rather than by drilling new ground. It was formed in 2021 by combining Contango Oil & Gas with KKR-backed Independence Energy, and it closed the purchase of Vital Energy's Permian assets on 2025-12-15 for about $3.1 billion including net debt, which the company described as accretive ([CRGY - Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm)). The current event is the same pattern, larger. On 2026-10-08, Devon Energy agreed to sell its Eagle Ford assets to Crescent for about $4.2 billion in cash, covering roughly 90,000 net acres; one report gives the purchase value as about $3.85 billion and cites roughly $140 million of annual cost savings ([Crescent Energy buys Devon Energy Eagle Ford assets for $4.2B and prices $1B equity offering (October 2026)](https://www.benzinga.com/m/26/10/62241109/devon-energy-sell-its-eagle-ford-assets-crescent-energy-4-2b-cash), [CRGY October 2026 Devon Eagle Ford purchase and Class A stock offering](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)). The same day the company started a $1 billion offering of Class A shares. It priced on 2026-10-09 at $12.50 a share for 80 million shares, and a KKR affiliate agreed to buy 40 million of them ([Crescent Energy $1B Class A common stock offering (2026-10-08)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm), [StockTitan: Crescent Energy prices 80M-share stock offering at $12.50](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)). One retained record links the offering proceeds to funding the Devon purchase. Another record says the reports do not state the use of proceeds or whether the 80 million shares are new shares, existing shares sold by holders, or a mix. **Reported results before the deal.** For the quarter that ended 2026-06-30, the supplied data show revenue of about $1.39 billion, net income of about $493 million and operating cash flow, the cash a business produces from normal operations, of about $944 million. Total assets were about $12.0 billion, total liabilities about $6.85 billion and shareholders' equity about $5.16 billion. The prior quarter, which ended 2026-03-31, showed a net loss of about $420 million on revenue of about $1.18 billion. The record does not explain what drove the swing between the two quarters. **The bullish hypothesis.** Mechanism: a repeat buyer of oil and gas assets gains scale in the Eagle Ford at a price that is cheaper than building the same production, and the reported cost savings lower the combined unit cost. Supporting facts: the consolidator model has a recent completed example (the Vital Energy Permian purchase, closed 2025-12-15), the $1 billion equity raise removes the need to fund the full cash price from the balance sheet alone, a KKR affiliate committed to half of the offered shares, and second-quarter 2026 results were strongly cash generative. Assumption: the acquisition earns more than its cost of capital and the equity issuance is small relative to the added cash flow. Counterevidence: no purchase agreement terms, no acquired production or reserve figures, no close date and no pro forma financials are in the evidence, so the claim that the deal is accretive cannot be tested. Invalidation: disclosure showing the purchase price per unit of production above comparable regional deals, or pro forma debt that is higher than before the deal without a path to reduce it. **The bearish hypothesis.** Mechanism: the company pays $4.2 billion in cash and sells 80 million new shares at $12.50 to help fund it, so each existing share now represents a smaller slice of the business and more debt. The stock has traded near the offering price since pricing: it closed at $12.84 on 2026-10-14 and fell 2.65% on 2026-10-15 ([CRGY - Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm)). Supporting facts: the 1-month return is -11.38% and the 1-week return is -7.20% as of 2026-10-15, and the deal report falls inside the 1-week window. Counterevidence: the 3-month return is +20.66%, so the shares are still well above where they started the quarter, and the 1-month window began around 2026-09-14, before the deal was announced, so the deal cannot explain the whole decline. Invalidation: a firm financing plan that holds pro forma debt near current levels, or evidence that per-share cash flow rises after the deal closes. **Which thesis the facts favor.** Neither has a clear edge. The decline is concentrated around a share sale and a large cash purchase, which is consistent with the bearish mechanism, but the same facts are equally consistent with a market that simply repriced the new share count. The bullish mechanism depends on deal economics that are not disclosed. Company identity is confirmed, the catalyst is dated and described, and the pre-deal results are solid on cash generation. Beyond that, the evidence does not settle the question, and guessing would be inventing an edge. **By horizon.** - **1 week:** driven by how the market absorbs the 80 million new shares and whether the stock holds near $12.50. No edge from the evidence. - **1 month:** driven by any further detail on funding, closing conditions and third-quarter results for the period ended 2026-09-30. No edge until those appear. - **3 month:** driven by whether the acquired assets add cash flow per share and whether debt falls. The 3-month return of +20.66% shows the market rewarded the equity earlier in this period, so the pullback is a partial give-back, not a full reversal. **Facts to obtain next.** The purchase agreement: total consideration, cash versus stock, debt financing, expected close date and conditions. The acquired production, reserves and cash flow, so the price can be compared with other Eagle Ford and Permian deals. Pro forma debt, earnings and per-share cash flow, plus share count before and after the offering. Whether the 80 million shares are newly issued. And the driver of the swing from the 2026-03-31 net loss to the 2026-06-30 net profit, including hedging and one-off items.

NVAX: # Novavax (NVAX) — research brief **As of 16 October 2026. Focus ticker only.** ## What the company is Novavax is a vaccine company. Its revenue now leans on partners who sell the product, plus milestone and royalty payments, rather than on large direct product sales of its own ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-novavax-nvax-stock-up-20-65-today-17829/)). A partnership payment changes cash and risk; it does not change commercial performance. ## The price move As of 15 October 2026 20:50 UTC, NVAX was up 14.3% over one week, 28.3% over one month and 62.6% over three months, and 1.3% on the day. Over five years it is down 92.3% (Market Explorer observation). A Zopedia snapshot at 9 October 2026 04:00 UTC put the close at $12.745. The 5-day return was +21.7%, the 21-day +36.9%, the 63-day +43.0%. The 14-day RSI was 68.1, near the 70 level that often marks an overbought market. The 20-day annualised volatility was 95%. Price sat about 90% up its recent channel, with resistance at $13.385 and support at $7.15 ([NVAX — Novavax](https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/NVAX/)). In the week of 5–7 October 2026, NVAX rose about 20%. Reports show a close of $12.56 on 5 October, up 20.08% on about 28.5 million shares; an intraday print of $12.12, up 15.9%, as a new 52-week high; and a print of $12.62, up 20.65%, about $2.16 above a prior close of $10.46. All three imply a prior close near $10.46, so they probably describe the same session at different times. One source shows an $11.01 close for 8 October, which does not agree with the $12.745 snapshot. The daily close series for 1–9 October 2026 is not settled ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-novavax-stock-surging-today-93CH-4932717)). ## Reported drivers Three causes are reported, not confirmed: - **An FDA-related catalyst.** An opened FDA page lists Nuvaxovid as approved, but the page is archived with an 08 July 2026 expiry. It does not confirm a new October 2026 action. - **A Sanofi agreement**, reported as a $500 million upfront payment, up to $700 million in future milestones, and royalties on future sales. This is the single most important number in the file. The exact terms, the 2026 triggers and the timing are not confirmed. - **Vaccine-sector strength.** Benzinga reported on 9–10 October 2026 that a new NIH-backed initiative to speed up personalised cancer vaccine development sent MRNA, BNTX and NVAX higher; live evidence says the NIH plans a public-private cancer vaccine programme starting in December, focused on pancreatic and liver cancer ([A New War on Cancer?](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally), [Vaccine Stocks Rally](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/vaccine-stocks-rally-reports-u-141200740.html)). On the same day, 24/7 Wall St reported NVAX at $12.77, up 16% (its own quick-read block said 14%), MRNA at $219.30, up 11%, MRK at $146.18, up 3%, the iShares Biotechnology ETF up 3% and SPY up 0.5% ([24/7 Wall St via AOL](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally)). ## What the company's own numbers show Period 2026Q1 (report date 31 March 2026): - Revenue $139.5 million, down 79.1% from a year earlier. The year-earlier quarter was far larger, and this revenue line is lumpy because it depends on partner payments and seasonal vaccine sales. - Net income -$9.5 million, against -$202.4 million in 2025Q3. - Operating cash flow -$32.4 million. - Free cash flow +$6.1 million, the first positive reading since 2025Q3. - Stockholders' equity -$144.8 million. - Total assets $1,043.2 million; total liabilities $1,187.9 million. Negative stockholders' equity has been the normal state since late 2021, with only brief positive readings. Liabilities have exceeded assets over the same period. Negative equity is a chronic condition, not a new one. ## Bull hypothesis **Mechanism.** Novavax has shifted from paying for its own manufacturing and sales to collecting partner payments. If the Sanofi agreement delivers a $500 million upfront, up to $700 million in milestones and a royalty stream, that cash arrives without a matching cost, which extends runway and makes revenue less dependent on the company's own commercial spending. At the same time, the net loss has narrowed sharply and free cash flow turned positive in 2026Q1. A group-level vaccine rally lifts the whole sector, and NVAX is a high-volatility member of it. **Supporting facts.** Price momentum is verified: +14.3% / +28.3% / +62.6% over one week, one month and three months. Sector news is dated and sourced. The reported Sanofi amounts are specific. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn and the narrower loss are in the supplied financials. Health Care led sectors on 15 October 2026. **Assumptions.** The reported Sanofi terms are real and paid on the described timetable. The October FDA item is a genuine new action, not a re-reading of an older approval. Novavax has a real role in the NIH programme, not just a sympathy bid. **Counterevidence.** The October catalysts are reported, not confirmed. The archived FDA page does not confirm a new action. No source shows Novavax as a participant in the NIH programme. Revenue still fell sharply and equity is negative. RSI at 68.1 and price 90% up the channel mean the move is extended. **Invalidation.** The bull case breaks if the Sanofi upfront or milestones are not confirmed and paid; if the October FDA action turns out to be a re-report of an older approval; if price falls back below the $10.46 prior close; if the NIH programme names participants and Novavax is not among them; or if the next filing shows free cash flow back in negative territory. ## Bear hypothesis **Mechanism.** The rally is a headline-and-sympathy move in a company whose commercial position has shrunk. Revenue is small and lumpy, and the balance sheet carries negative equity. Any financing — equity issuance or convertible debt — would dilute existing holders, in a stock that already lost 92.3% over five years. Subsiding momentum in a 95%-volatility name can reverse quickly, and a cancer-vaccine headline does not transfer unless the company has a cancer-vaccine product. **Supporting facts.** Five-year return -92.3%. 2026Q1 revenue $139.5 million, down 79.1% year over year. Operating cash flow -$32.4 million. Stockholders' equity -$144.8 million. Liabilities ($1,187.9 million) exceed assets ($1,043.2 million). Annualised volatility 95%. RSI 68.1. No analyst data, share count, cash balance or free float was retrieved. **Assumptions.** Partner and royalty payments are not enough to fund the business at its current cost level. The sector rally fades. No new company-specific positive event arrives. **Counterevidence.** A large, low-cost Sanofi cash inflow is exactly what the bear case must explain away. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn and the narrower loss are early evidence against a permanent cash-burn view. The group bid from the NIH headline was real on the day, and Health Care led sectors on 15 October 2026. **Invalidation.** The bear case breaks if the Sanofi payment is confirmed and received; if the next filing shows growth in partner and royalty revenue; if free cash flow stays positive for a second quarter; if the company raises cash without issuing equity; or if short-interest data shows the rally was a squeeze that has now cleared. ## Which thesis the facts favour Over one week to one month, the facts favour the bull case on momentum and sector direction, because those two things are verified and point the same way. The edge is thin, not strong: the company-specific catalysts are reported rather than confirmed, and the price is extended inside its channel. Over three months, the question is whether the Sanofi money and the 2026–2027 COVID season actually land. This file does not settle that. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn is the only company-specific datapoint pointing bullish; the revenue fall and negative equity point the other way. Neither side has a supportable edge at that horizon from this evidence. Over five years, the record is clearly negative at -92.3%, and nothing in this file shows a product that reverses it. I would not claim a bullish edge at that horizon. ## Facts to obtain next - The Sanofi agreement's exact upfront amount, milestone schedule, royalty rate and 2026 triggers. - The exact FDA action behind the 5–6 October 2026 move, and whether Nuvaxovid's approval was renewed or extended after 8 July 2026. - The current cash and short-term investments balance, share count, and any at-the-market or other financing. - Whether Novavax is named in the NIH personalised cancer vaccine programme. - Analyst estimate revisions and price targets after 9 October 2026. - Short interest and free float, to test whether a squeeze produced the move. - A reconciled daily close series for 1–9 October 2026.

# Strive, Inc. — Class A Common Stock (ASST)

## Identity

Strive, Inc. trades on Nasdaq under the ticker ASST. Its investor relations page says that after a merger in September 2025 it became the first publicly traded asset management Bitcoin Treasury Corporation, and it calls itself a structured finance company. The ASST ticker belonged to Asset Entities Inc. before that combination, so prices from before September 2025 are not comparable with later prices.

The company holds bitcoin on its balance sheet, sells asset management services, and sells bitcoin-linked preferred stock. Fair-value accounting requires it to show bitcoin at its current market value, so reported earnings move with the bitcoin price.

## Bitcoin holdings

On 2026-10-13 Strive reported that it bought 3,311 bitcoin for about $280 million between 5 and 9 October 2026, at an average of about $84,500 per coin. That lifted holdings to 32,773 bitcoin ([Benzinga, 2026-10-13](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62320971/strive-acquires-3-311-bitcoins-average-price-84-500-bitcoin-oct-5-through-oct-9); [Benzinga, 2026-10-13](https://benzinga.com/crypto/cryptocurrency/26/10/62332544/saylor-cheers-strives-280-million-bitcoin-buy-while-strategy-bought-85-less)).

Earlier weekly reports: 469 bitcoin at about $77,954 each between 8 and 11 September 2026, which took holdings to 25,000 bitcoin ([Cryptonews.net](https://cryptonews.net/news/bitcoin/33442634)); 1,355 bitcoin at about $79,475 each in the week of 14 to 18 September 2026; and 1,107 bitcoin at about $85,396 each in the week of 21 to 25 September 2026 (retained Zopedia market-event page on the weekly purchase reports).

The reported weekly amounts do not fully account for the stated total. The three weeks reported after the 25,000 level add 5,773 bitcoin, but holdings rose 7,773 bitcoin, from 25,000 to 32,773. At least one week is missing from the retained reports. The company also did not state how it paid for the bitcoin, so the funding channel is unknown.

## Funding: preferred shares

On 2026-10-13 Strive announced a planned initial public offering of 5 million SATS preferred shares at $100 each, to raise $500 million. SATS would pay a fixed 15% dividend and rank behind the existing SATA preferred series, which pays a variable rate that is currently 13% ([Coindesk, 2026-10-13](https://coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/13/strive-to-ipo-second-preferred-share-class-as-it-looks-to-further-build-bitcoin-treasury); [Benzinga, 2026-10-13](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62341031/strive-plans-conduct-initial-public-offering-of-5m-shares-its-15-series-perpetual-sats-preferred-shares)). The company said it would use the money for more bitcoin, income-producing assets, or share buybacks. The offering was not complete as of 2026-10-16.

The preferred layer matters for the common stock. SATA at about 13% plus SATS at 15% would take about $75 million a year in dividends before a common holder receives anything. Paying for bitcoin with preferred stock raises the amount of bitcoin behind each common share only if the return on bitcoin beats the dividend cost.

## Price move

The shared market observation for 2026-10-15 shows ASST up 3.89% on the day and up 107.7% over three months, tagged "Up / cooling". The tag means the earlier gain is slowing, not reversing. # CORZ — Core Scientific, Inc. Common Stock

## Identity
Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) mines bitcoin and rents high-density data-center space. The rental business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI (artificial intelligence) and HPC (high-performance computing) customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024.

## Merger history (one conflicting date)
CoreWeave agreed to buy Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (company press release). That deal did not complete. One retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination date as unverified until a filing or press release confirms it. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ.

## Reported results, quarter ended 30 June 2026
- Revenue: $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M one year earlier.
- Operating income: +$20.7M. Gross profit: $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA: $41.1M. Liquidity: $1.82B.
- Total assets: $5.26B, up from $3.07B at 31 March 2026. Total liabilities: $7.68B, up from $4.38B.
- Stockholders' equity: -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are larger than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event.
- Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026, which points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss.

## Cash flow
The free cash flow figure was -$1.02B in Q2 2026, and this is a quarterly number. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive, so most of the outflow is capital spending. That one quarter is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025.

## Funding and pipeline
- $3.3B of 7.75% senior secured notes, described in the Q1 2026 results release.
- $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities, reported 14 September 2026.
- Conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data-center sites, reported 14 September 2026. ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions.
- AMD partnership announced 28 July 2026: 500+ MW (megawatts, a unit of power) of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW (gigawatts, 1,000 megawatts).

## Price action and its driver
On 15 October 2026 CORZ rose 7.1% on the day, but it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months and -27.5% over one year. Two retained price points for 7-8 October conflict: one reports a $15.94 price on 2026-10-07 and another reports a close of $18.10 on 2026-10-08. Neither should be used.

The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders, not a CORZ-specific operating failure. On 7-8 October 2026 Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose. Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion. The only company-specific October item found is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05), which is too small to explain the decline.

## Competing forward-looking theses as of 15 October 2026
Bull case: converting low-cost power and land into high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin, and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The assumption to test is that announcements become signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt.

Bear case: a capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow; $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets; negative equity.

Neither side has a clean edge at one week or one month, because direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates. At three months and one year the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating.

## Facts to obtain next
- The CoreWeave deal termination date.
- Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity, with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates.
- The Q3 2026 report date and results.
- Leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.

# Moderna (MRNA) — business facts and three-horizon outlook, October 2026

As of 15 October 2026. Established facts are separated from forward hypotheses. The forward parts are analysis, not reported results.

## What the company sells

Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRNA) is a commercial-stage maker of mRNA vaccines. Approved products are Spikevax for COVID-19, mRESVIA for RSV, and mFLUSIVA for seasonal influenza. The FDA approved mFLUSIVA on 5 August 2026, after a unanimous advisory-committee vote in June 2026.

The most valuable pipeline asset is intismeran autogene, also called mRNA-4157 or V940. It is a personalised cancer vaccine that Moderna develops with Merck. The norovirus candidate mRNA-1403 did not meet statistical criteria at a Phase 3 interim analysis.

Revenue is seasonal. COVID and RSV vaccine sales rise in fall and winter, so Q3 and Q4 carry the year.

## Reported results for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 (reported 31 July 2026)

- Revenue $145 million, up 2.1% from a year earlier.
- Net loss $782 million. Operating cash flow -$526 million. Free cash flow -$563 million.
- Stockholders' equity $6.76 billion against $4.20 billion of liabilities.
- The company cut its 2026 cost and research outlook, repeated a plan for up to 10% revenue growth, and guided to $4.7–5.2 billion of year-end cash.

Read these numbers with seasonality in mind. Q2 2026 revenue of $145 million and first-half revenue of $534 million say little about the full year, because Q3 2025 revenue was $1,016 million. The next report is expected on 6 November 2026.

## Financing and cash

- 27 August 2026: Moderna proposed a private placement of $2.0 billion of convertible senior notes.
- 28 August 2026: the company priced an upsized $2.6 billion offering and filed an 8-K on 1 September 2026.
- Net proceeds were about $2.957 billion after full exercise of the purchasers' option. The company spent $328.8 million on capped calls. Cash and investments were $6.9 billion at 30 June 2026, before a $950 million litigation payment.
- One secondary report describes $3.0 billion of zero-coupon notes due 2032. The retained filing record does not give the coupon, maturity or conversion terms.

## The price move and its reported drivers

MRNA closed at $221.16 on 9 October 2026. It was about 14% higher that day, +61.9% over 21 days, and +230.1% over 63 days, with a 14-day RSI of 71.2 and 20% annualised volatility of 80.5%. It remained 54.4% below its $484.65 all-time high. Supplied observations for 15 October 2026 show +4.82% on the day, +297.4% over three months, +753.3% over one year, and -22.5% over five years. A separate 15 October record puts the day at +5.52%.

At least three reported drivers ran in sequence:

1. 19 August 2026 — Merck and Moderna announced positive topline Phase 3 results for intismeran autogene plus KEYTRUDA in completely resected Stage IIB-IV melanoma. The INTerpath-001 trial met recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival endpoints. Press coverage credits this result with nearly doubling the stock.
2. 1 October 2026 — Nasdaq said MRNA would rejoin the Nasdaq-100 before the open on 9 October 2026, replacing Warner Bros. Discovery. This creates real, one-time index-fund buying.
3. 9 October 2026 — a National Institutes of Health-backed public-private cancer-vaccine programme lifted MRNA, BioNTech and Novavax. It targets pancreatic, liver and colorectal cancers first and is expected to start in December 2026. No revenue attaches to it yet.

A separate 6 October 2026 report says MRNA fell about 7% after a World Health Organization update.

## Competing forward hypotheses (analysis, not established fact)

**Three months, to mid-January 2027.** Bull mechanism: the 6 November Q3 report should show the seasonal step-up toward the roughly $1 billion Q3 2025 level, and mFLUSIVA adds a third approved product into the same fall window. Bear mechanism: the October gain came from index buying and from a programme that starts in December; momentum is stretched above RSI 70; the company still consumes cash; and the $950 million litigation payment falls in this window. Counterevidence for the bear case: the August 2026 convertible raise removes near-term funding stress. Verdict: the tape changed but the operating facts did not, so neither side has a reliable price edge. Invalidation tests: Q3 revenue materially below $1 billion or a guidance cut on 6 November (bear); a Q3 beat with a raised outlook, or a regulatory filing acceptance for intismeran autogene (bull).

**One year, to October 2027.** Bull mechanism: a Phase 3 that met two endpoints in high-risk resected melanoma supports a regulatory submission in 2027, which would add a high-price oncology line and shift the mix away from seasonal vaccines. Merck brings an existing checkpoint-inhibitor franchise and commercial reach. Bear mechanism: even an approval would be a small, slow revenue line against a shrinking COVID franchise, and the pipeline also carries failures. Verdict: the established facts favour the bull case. The bear case at this horizon rests mainly on valuation and on how quickly oncology revenue arrives, which is unknown. Invalidation: a regulatory delay or negative review, or no filing for intismeran autogene by mid-2027.

**Five years, to 2031.** Bull mechanism: if mRNA works in oncology, the platform addresses many tumour types, and the NIH programme plus Merck's pipeline widen the market. Bear mechanism: equity fell from $11.9 billion in 2024Q3 to $6.76 billion in 2026Q2; the company has raised capital repeatedly; and reimbursement and manufacturing economics for personalised neoantigen therapy at scale are unproven. Verdict: neither thesis has an edge yet.

## Open questions

- What the late-October 2026 late-stage melanoma presentation contains, and whether it is the INTerpath-001 dataset or a new one.
- The coupon, maturity and conversion terms of the August 2026 convertible notes, and the dilution they imply.
- The status and cash effect of the $950 million litigation matter, because the $6.9 billion cash figure at 30 June 2026 predates it.
- Whether Merck has filed for approval of intismeran autogene.
- Whether the NIH cancer-vaccine programme creates procurement that reaches Moderna specifically.

All amounts are in US dollars. Quarterly figures are calendar quarters. The rally percentages are price returns over the stated windows and are not comparable across sources when the end-date snapshot differs.

ticker_packages.answer_markdown: Strive, Inc. (Nasdaq: ASST) is a company that holds bitcoin on its balance sheet — a "bitcoin treasury" company — and also sells asset-management services. The ASST ticker belonged to Asset Entities Inc. before a merger in September 2025, so share prices from before that date are not comparable with today's. Accounting rules also require Strive to report bitcoin at its current market value, so reported earnings swing with the bitcoin price. On 2026-10-15 the shares rose 3.89%, and over three months they are up 107.7%. The screen tag "Up / cooling" means the earlier gain is slowing, not reversing. **The bullish mechanism.** Strive pays for bitcoin mostly with preferred stock — a class of share that pays a fixed dividend and ranks ahead of common stock for payouts — instead of issuing new common shares. That avoids diluting the common shares (spreading ownership thinner) and raises the amount of bitcoin behind each common share, as long as bitcoin's return beats the dividend cost. Two things support this. First, Strive bought 3,311 bitcoin for about $280 million at roughly $84,500 per coin between 5 and 9 October 2026, taking holdings to 32,773 bitcoin ([Strive Acquires 3,311 Bitcoins At Average Price Of $84,500 Per Bitcoin From Oct. 5 Through Oct. 9](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62320971/strive-acquires-3-311-bitcoins-average-price-84-500-bitcoin-oct-5-through-oct-9)). Second, it announced — but has not completed — an initial public offering of 5 million SATS preferred shares at $100 each, to raise $500 million, paying a 15% dividend and ranking behind the existing SATA preferred ([Strive Plans To Conduct Initial Public Offering Of 5M Shares Of Its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Shares](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62341031/strive-plans-conduct-initial-public-offering-5m-shares-its-15-series-perpetual-sats-preferred-shares); [Strive (ASST) aims to raise $500 million with SATS preferred offering](https://coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/13/strive-to-ipo-second-preferred-share-class-as-it-looks-to-further-build-bitcoin-treasury)). SATA pays about 13% (variable) and SATS would pay 15%, so together they would absorb roughly $75 million a year in fixed dividends before a common holder receives anything. If bitcoin is flat or falls, the leftover value tilts to the preferred holders. Three facts cut against the bull case. The weekly regulatory filings do not add up: the reported weeks sum to about 6,242 bitcoin, short of the 7,773-coin increase in holdings, so one report is missing, and the source of the money used to buy the bitcoin is not disclosed. The number that settles the question is bitcoin per ASST share after the purchases and the raise, compared with the share price. If the shares cost less than the bitcoin behind them, that is a discount; if they cost more, that is a premium. The bear thesis fails if bitcoin rallies well past recent purchase prices, or if the proceeds are held or used for buybacks rather than spent. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, but the bull case is not disproved. The decisive year-ahead question is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases.** **Company identity.** Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) is a bitcoin miner that now sells high-density data-center space. That business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI and high-performance computing customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024. CoreWeave agreed to acquire Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (CoreWeave to acquire Core Scientific, company press release). That deal did not complete. A retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination timing as unverified. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ. **Price move.** On 15 October 2026, CORZ rose 7.1% on the day. But it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months, and -27.5% over one year. The day's gain came against a falling semiconductor and AI-hardware tape driven by rate-hike fears (Rate Pressure vs. AI Demand: Rising Treasury Yields Trigger Nvidia, AMD Slump). Similar single-day gains in Cipher and TeraWulf look like a catalyst-free oversold bounce. Treat 15 October as group mean-reversion in beaten-down miner and data-center names until a company-specific driver appears. Do not use the 7-8 October price points in the retained snippets: one says CORZ fell 4.4% to $15.94 on 2026-10-07, another says it closed down 3.67% at $18.10 on 2026-10-08. These cannot both be right, so no price level should be taken from them. **Shared driver, not company failure.** The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders. On 7-8 October, Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose ([IREN Falls 7% as Financing-Heavy Data Center Names Sell Off Apart From Their Sector Fund; TeraWulf and Core Scientific Drop 5%](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/07/iren-falls-7-as-financing-heavy-data-center-names-sell-off-apart-from-their-sector-fund-terawulf-and-core-scientific-drop-5)). This matters because Core Scientific must borrow to build. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion ([Capital Over Chips: Broadcom CEO Warns Financing Costs Could Slow AI Expansion](https://benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62379402/capital-over-chips-broadcom-ceo-warns-financing-costs-could-slow-ai-expansion)). **Reported results for the quarter ended 2026-06-30.** Revenue was $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M a year earlier. Liquidity was $1.82B ([Core Scientific Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/139/core-scientific-announces-second-quarter-2026-results)). The build-out is the dominant financial fact: total assets rose to $5.26B from $3.07B at 31 March 2026, and total liabilities rose to $7.68B from $4.38B. **Read the cash flow correctly.** Free cash flow was -$1.02B in Q2 2026. That single quarter's outflow is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025. ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions. **Negative equity.** Stockholders' equity was -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are greater than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event. Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026. That swing points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss. The binding constraints are liquidity and continued access to debt and equity on acceptable terms. **Bull case, mechanism and support.** Core Scientific owns low-cost power and land. Converting it to high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt and per dollar invested once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin. On 28 July 2026, the company announced an AMD partnership covering 500+ MW of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW. MW means megawatt, a unit of power. GW means gigawatt, 1,000 megawatts. ERCOT conditional approvals support the Texas pipeline. Assumption: the pipeline becomes signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt. Invalidation: announcements do not turn into contracts with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates; or leasing rents and utilization fall short of the cost of capital. **Bear case, mechanism and support.** A capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. That sale is too small to explain the decline. **Verdict by horizon.** For one week and one month, neither side has a clean edge. The direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates, which the company does not control. Note that Q2 2026 results were reported on 28 July 2026, so a Q3 2026 report is likely within the one-month window, even though the confirmed date is not in the evidence. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The decisive variable over a year is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases. **What to obtain next.** The CoreWeave deal termination date. Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates. The Q3 2026 report date and results. # CORZ — Core Scientific, Inc. Common Stock

## Identity
Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) mines bitcoin and rents high-density data-center space. The rental business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI (artificial intelligence) and HPC (high-performance computing) customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024.

## Merger history (one conflicting date)
CoreWeave agreed to buy Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (company press release). That deal did not complete. One retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination date as unverified until a filing or press release confirms it. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ.

## Reported results, quarter ended 30 June 2026
- Revenue: $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M one year earlier.
- Operating income: +$20.7M. Gross profit: $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA: $41.1M. Liquidity: $1.82B.
- Total assets: $5.26B, up from $3.07B at 31 March 2026. Total liabilities: $7.68B, up from $4.38B.
- Stockholders' equity: -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are larger than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event.
- Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026, which points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss.

## Cash flow
The free cash flow figure was -$1.02B in Q2 2026, and this is a quarterly number. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive, so most of the outflow is capital spending. That one quarter is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025.

## Funding and pipeline
- $3.3B of 7.75% senior secured notes, described in the Q1 2026 results release.
- $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities, reported 14 September 2026.
- Conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data-center sites, reported 14 September 2026. ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions.
- AMD partnership announced 28 July 2026: 500+ MW (megawatts, a unit of power) of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW (gigawatts, 1,000 megawatts).

## Price action and its driver
On 15 October 2026 CORZ rose 7.1% on the day, but it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months and -27.5% over one year. Two retained price points for 7-8 October conflict: one reports a $15.94 price on 2026-10-07 and another reports a close of $18.10 on 2026-10-08. Neither should be used.

The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders, not a CORZ-specific operating failure. On 7-8 October 2026 Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose. Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion. The only company-specific October item found is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05), which is too small to explain the decline.

## Competing forward-looking theses as of 15 October 2026
Bull case: converting low-cost power and land into high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin, and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The assumption to test is that announcements become signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt.

Bear case: a capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow; $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets; negative equity.

Neither side has a clean edge at one week or one month, because direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates. At three months and one year the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating.

## Facts to obtain next
- The CoreWeave deal termination date.
- Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity, with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates.
- The Q3 2026 report date and results.
- Leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.
